_meta.indication: FYCOMPA (perampanel) is indicated as adjunctive therapy for the treatment of partial-onset seizures with or without secondarily generalized seizures in patients with epilepsy aged 12 years and older.

pivotal_trials.design: Multiple fixed-dose, double-blind, multi-center, placebo-controlled study; patients randomized to target perampanel 8 or 12 mg/day once daily or placebo, after a 6-week baseline phase with 6-week titration.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 12 years and older with refractory partial-onset seizures
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Median percent change from baseline in seizure frequency (per 28 days) during the maintenance phase
pivotal_trials.n: 388 randomized (placebo 121, peram 8 mg 133, peram 12 mg 134); mITT analysis population: placebo 121, 8 mg 133, 12 mg 133
pivotal_trials.result: mITT median % change from baseline: -21 (placebo), -26.3 (8 mg, p=0.026), -34.5 (12 mg, p=0.016)

pivotal_trials.design: Same protocol and design as Study 304 (double-blind, placebo-controlled; target perampanel 8 or 12 mg/day vs placebo)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 12 years and older with refractory partial-onset seizures
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Median percent change from baseline in seizure frequency (per 28 days) during the maintenance phase (same primary endpoint as Study 304, which used the same protocol and design)
pivotal_trials.result: mITT median % change from baseline: -9.7 (placebo), -30.5 (8 mg, p=0.0008), -17.6 (12 mg, p=.01)

pivotal_trials.design: Similar design to Studies 304 and 305 (6-week prospective baseline, 6-week titration phase, 13-week maintenance phase); patients randomized to placebo or perampanel 2, 4, or 8 mg/day.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 12 years and older with refractory partial-onset seizures
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Median percent change from baseline in seizure frequency (per 28 days) during the maintenance phase (same primary endpoint as Studies 304/305, whose design this study followed)
pivotal_trials.result: mITT median % change from baseline: -10.7 (placebo), -13.6 (2 mg, p=0.4), -23.3 (4 mg, p=0.003), -30.8 (8 mg, p<0.0001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=4% and >=1% higher than placebo) include dizziness, somnolence, fatigue, irritability, falls, nausea, weight gain, vertigo, ataxia, gait disturbance, and balance disorder. Dizziness occurred in 9% (placebo), 16% (4 mg), 32% (8 mg), and 43% (12 mg). Serious or life-threatening psychiatric and behavioral reactions including aggression, hostility, and homicidal ideation have been reported.
target_moa: Perampanel is a non-competitive antagonist of the AMPA glutamate receptor; the mechanism of action in epilepsy is not fully established.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SERIOUS PSYCHIATRIC AND BEHAVIORAL REACTIONS — serious or life-threatening psychiatric and behavioral adverse reactions including aggression, hostility, irritability, anger, and homicidal ideation and threats have been reported in patients taking FYCOMPA.

rems.type: A REMS has not been proposed by the Sponsor and FDA agreed that a REMS is not necessary.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical study design is similar to previously approved products in the class.

summary.text: NDA 202834 was submitted under section 505(b) and received 12/22/11 for perampanel as adjunctive therapy for partial-onset seizures in patients aged 12 and older; it was approved 10/22/2012 and was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical study design is similar to previously approved products in the class. The product's controlled substance scheduling was still proceeding at the time of approval.

requirement.text: 1932-1: A pharmacokinetic study in pediatric patients with partial-onset seizures aged 1 month to <24 months, evaluating at least 2 maintenance dose levels of FYCOMPA.

citations.quote: 1932-1 A pharmacokinetic study in pediatric patients with partial-onset seizures aged 1 month to < 24 months. At least 2 maintenance dose levels of FYCOMPA (perampanel) should be evaluated to characterize pharmacokinetic parameters following multiple administration of oral perampanel. Pharmacokinetic data can be obtained and analyzed using either conventional pharmacokinetics methods with intensive sampling or using a population PK approach by collecting sparse samples. Subjects should be balanced among age cohorts. Effort should also be made to balance the gender distributions within each age cohort.
